topic: Advanced tax law within VITA/TCE scope

notes.front: What is the Simplified Method?
notes.back: The method used to work out the tax-free portion of each pension or annuity payment, from the taxpayer's cost basis.
notes.explanation: Unless an exception applies, retirees must use it for annuity payments from a qualified plan; the other method is the General Rule.
notes.example: Like spreading the cost of a season ticket over the number of matches, so each match carries an equal share of what you already paid.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 142
notes.evidence: The Simplified Method is used to calculate the tax-free portion of each pension or annuity payment.

notes.front: What is the five-year test period suspension for a home sale?
notes.back: An election to suspend the five-year ownership and use test period while the homeowner serves on qualified official extended duty.
notes.explanation: It covers members of the uniformed services or Foreign Service, intelligence community employees, and Peace Corps employees or volunteers.
notes.example: Like stopping the clock in a match while a player is off the pitch, so their time away does not count against them.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Capital Gain or Loss”, PDF p. 132
notes.evidence: Taxpayers can choose to have the five-year test period for ownership and use suspended during any period the homeowner (either spouse if married) served on “qualified official extended duty” as a member of the uniformed services or Foreign Service of the United States,

notes.front: What is the IRA self-certification procedure?
notes.back: A procedure (Revenue Procedure 2016-47) letting people who missed the 60-day rollover limit by mistake self-certify for a waiver.
notes.explanation: Eligible taxpayers can qualify for a waiver and avoid possible taxes and penalties on early distributions.
notes.example: Like a signed note to the library explaining that a postal strike, not you, made the book late, which the library ordinarily accepts.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 141
notes.evidence: Revenue Procedure 2016-47 explains a self-certification procedure designed to help recipients of retirement plan distributions who inadvertently miss the 60-day time limit for properly rolling these amounts into another retirement plan or individual retirement arrangement (IRA).

notes.front: Which certification level can prepare the limited Schedule C?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The software works out net profit once income and expenses are entered.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 105
notes.evidence: Volunteer tax preparers who have Advanced certification can assist with preparation of the limited Schedule C.

notes.front: A Schedule C is in scope only if the business has less than {{c1::$50,000}} in business expenses.
notes.explanation: The scope chart states the same limit the other way round: total expenses over $50,000 are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: Volunteers can assist taxpayers who have returns that require Schedule C with certain limits: • Have less than $50,000 in business expenses

notes.front: Which method of accounting must an in-scope Schedule C business use?
notes.back: The cash method.
notes.explanation: Under the cash method, income is reported when received and expenses deducted when paid.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: The cash method of accounting reports all income when received and deducts all expenses when paid.

notes.front: A Schedule C business had inventory for part of the year. Is it in scope?
notes.back: No. There must be no inventory at any time during the year.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers with inventories are referred to a professional tax preparer.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: Inventory is the items the taxpayer buys or makes for resale to others. Taxpayers with inventories should be referred to a professional tax preparer.

notes.front: Can volunteers prepare a Schedule C showing a net loss?
notes.back: No. The business must not have had a net loss.
notes.explanation: Carryover losses from another year are also out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 13
notes.evidence: Business use of home • Net losses • Carryover losses from another year

notes.front: A sole proprietor paid an employee, or paid for contract labour. Is the Schedule C in scope?
notes.back: No. There must be no employees and no contract labour.
notes.explanation: Both are listed among the Schedule C limits in Publication 4491.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: Have no employees during the year and did not pay contract labor for services (out of scope issue)

notes.front: Which Schedule C costs, spread over years, put the return out of scope?
notes.back: Depreciation, and the election to expense business assets: anything needing Form 4562.
notes.explanation: A de minimis expense election is the exception Publication 4491 points to.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: Are not required to file Form 4562, Depreciation and Amortization, for this business (depreciation and the election to expense business assets are out of scope for the VITA/TCE programs),

notes.front: A self-employed taxpayer wants to deduct expenses for business use of the home. Is that in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Business use of the home is one of the Schedule C limits.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: Do not deduct expenses for business use of a home

notes.front: Which certification does income on Form 1099-NEC need, and who is excluded?
notes.back: Advanced; anyone receiving name, image and likeness income, such as athletes, is out of scope.
notes.explanation: The scope chart lists nonemployee compensation as in scope with Advanced certification.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: F 1099-NEC Yes Nonemployee compensation Advanced Certification

notes.front: Which Form 1099-K income is in scope, and at what level?
notes.back: Self-employment income, such as shared-economy driving, at Advanced; rental income only with Military certification.
notes.explanation: Forms 1099-K for any other type of taxable income are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: F 1099-K Yes Payment Card and Third Party Network Transactions Advanced certification In scope for:

notes.front: Which certification does self-employment tax (Schedule 2, line 4) need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The deductible part of self-employment tax on Schedule 1 also needs Advanced.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: S2 4 Yes Self-employment tax Advanced certification

notes.front: A taxpayer sold mutual fund shares. Which certification does the return need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: Capital gain distributions alone are Basic; a sale of shares needs Schedule D or Form 8949.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Interest and Dividends”, PDF p. 98
notes.evidence: A volunteer must have Advanced certification to prepare a return for taxpayers who sold mutual fund shares or other shares of stock.

notes.front: Which kinds of asset sale are in scope on Schedule D?
notes.back: Only stocks, mutual funds, exchange-traded funds and a personal residence.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers who sold any other kind of asset are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Taxpayers who sold any assets other than stocks, mutual funds, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), or a personal residence

notes.front: Is Form 1099-DA, Digital Asset Proceeds From Broker Transactions, in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The scope chart marks it No at every level.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: F 1099-DA No Digital Asset Proceeds From Broker Transactions

notes.front: A taxpayer sold cryptocurrency this year. Is the capital gain in scope?
notes.back: No. Transactions using digital assets are out of scope on Schedule D.
notes.explanation: Only a taxpayer who can check No to the Form 1040 digital asset question is in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Taxpayers who have transactions using digital assets. If the taxpayer can check the No box to the digital asset question on Form 1040, the return is in scope.

notes.front: Which certification does a home sale reported on Form 1099-S need, and for which property?
notes.back: Advanced, and only for a personal residence.
notes.explanation: A home used for rental, business property, installment sales and like-kind exchanges are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 18
notes.evidence: F 1099-S Yes Proceeds from Real Estate Transactions Advanced certification In scope for: required • Personal residence

notes.front: A taxpayer sells a home that was once rented out. Is the sale in scope?
notes.back: No. A home used for rental purposes is out of scope.
notes.explanation: Depreciation while the home was rented is also out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 18
notes.evidence: Home was used for rental purposes

notes.front: For the five-year test period suspension, when is a taxpayer on qualified official extended duty?
notes.back: When serving at a duty station at least 50 miles from the main home, or living in government quarters under government order.
notes.explanation: The duty must also be for more than 90 days or an indefinite period.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Capital Gain or Loss”, PDF p. 132
notes.evidence: Taxpayers are on qualified official extended duty if they serve at a duty station at least 50 miles from their main home or live in government quarters under government order.

notes.front: How long can the five-year test period suspension last, and on how many properties at once?
notes.back: No more than ten years, making up to fifteen years with the test period; one property at a time.
notes.explanation: The extension can also help taxpayers who have recently left the military.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Capital Gain or Loss”, PDF p. 132
notes.evidence: The period of suspension cannot last more than ten years. Together, the ten-year suspension period and the five-year test period can be as long as fifteen years. The suspension can be used on only one property at a time.

notes.front: Which method must retirees use to find the taxable part of annuity payments from a qualified plan?
notes.back: The Simplified Method, unless an exception applies.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers with after-tax contributions have basis in the plan, which they recover a bit at a time.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 142
notes.evidence: Unless an exception applies, retirees must use the Simplified Method for annuity payments from a qualified plan.

notes.front: A taxpayer says they have used the General Rule for their pension in past years. What does the volunteer do?
notes.back: Refer them to a professional tax preparer.
notes.explanation: The scope chart lists taxpayers who used the General Rule in past years as out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 142
notes.evidence: If a taxpayer tells you they have been using the General Rule to figure the taxable portion for past years, refer them to a professional tax preparer.

notes.front: Under the Simplified Method, the monthly tax-free portion is the taxpayer's cost basis divided by the {{c1::number of monthly payments}}.
notes.back: number of monthly payments
notes.explanation: The number of payments depends on the taxpayer's age (and the spouse's, for a joint and survivor annuity) at the annuity start date.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 142
notes.evidence: Taxpayer’s cost basis ÷ Number of monthly payments = Monthly Tax-Free Portion

notes.front: Name two circumstances that ordinarily qualify a late rollover for a self-certified waiver?
notes.back: For example, a distribution cheque that was misplaced and never cashed; a postal error.
notes.explanation: Revenue Procedure 2016-47 lists others, among them a financial institution's error, serious illness and a family member's death.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 141
notes.evidence: The distribution was in the form of a check and the check was misplaced and never cashed.

notes.front: Which certification does a qualified charitable distribution from Form 1099-R need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The intake sheet codes the item (A).
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (A) Qualified Charitable Distribution From 1099-R

notes.front: Is Form 8606, Nondeductible IRAs, in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Nondeductible traditional IRA contributions are also out of scope on the IRA deduction line.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: F 8606 No Nondeductible IRAs

notes.front: For the additional tax on IRAs and retirement plans (Form 5329), which level is needed?
notes.back: Basic if the additional tax applies; Advanced if an exception to it applies.
notes.explanation: Only Part I of Form 5329 is in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: S2 8 Yes Additional tax on IRAs, other qualified retirement plans, and other tax-favored Basic certification if accounts additional tax applies

notes.front: Which Form 5329 situations are out of scope?
notes.back: Excess IRA contributions not withdrawn by the return's due date, IRA minimum distributions not taken, and Parts II to IX.
notes.explanation: Only Part I of the form is in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 19
notes.evidence: IRA minimum distributions not withdrawn when required • Excess contributions to an IRA that are not withdrawn by the due date of the return including extensions • Parts II through IX

notes.front: Which IRA contributions can be deducted on an in-scope return, and at what level?
notes.back: Deductible traditional IRA contributions, at Advanced; nondeductible ones are out of scope.
notes.explanation: The scope chart splits traditional IRA contributions into these two groups.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: S1 20 Yes IRA deduction Advanced certification In scope for: required • Deductible traditional IRA contributions Not in scope for: • Nondeductible traditional IRA contributions

notes.front: Which certification does a health savings account (Form 8889) need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The HSA deduction on Schedule 1 carries the same requirement.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: S1 13 Yes Health savings account deduction Advanced certification

notes.front: Name two HSA situations that are out of scope?
notes.back: Excess contributions not withdrawn in time; a qualified HSA funding distribution from an IRA.
notes.explanation: Among others, Part III (failure to keep high deductible plan coverage) is also out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 21
notes.evidence: Excess contributions to an HSA that are not withdrawn in a timely fashion • Qualified HSA funding distributions from an IRA

notes.front: When is the self-employed health insurance deduction out of scope?
notes.back: When the insurance was bought through the Marketplace and the taxpayer is eligible for the premium tax credit.
notes.explanation: Otherwise the deduction is in scope with Advanced certification.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Insurance purchased through Marketplace when taxpayer is eligible for Premium Tax Credit

notes.front: Which certification do the premium tax credit (Form 8962) and Form 1095-A need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The scope chart lists both with Advanced certification required.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: F 1095-A Yes Health Insurance Marketplace Statement Advanced certification required

notes.front: Which certification does repaying excess advance premium tax credit (Schedule 2, line 1a) need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: Other lines of Schedule 2, line 1 are out of scope unless the training covers them.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: In scope for: Advanced certification • Line a, Excess advance premium tax credit repayment required
uses: advance payments of the premium tax credit

notes.front: Which certification do itemized deductions on Schedule A need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: Schedule A also carries its own list of out-of-scope items.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 13
notes.evidence: SA Yes Itemized Deductions Advanced certification

notes.front: Name two Schedule A items that are out of scope?
notes.back: Casualty or theft losses; donations of motor vehicles, boats or aeroplanes (Form 1098-C).
notes.explanation: Among others, investment interest and donations of capital gain property are also out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 13
notes.evidence: Form 1098-C, Contributions of Motor Vehicles, Boats and Airplanes • Donation of property previously depreciated • Donation of capital gain property (such as securities or art work) • Casualty or theft losses

notes.front: What limit applies to noncash charitable contributions on an in-scope return?
notes.back: $500 or less at Advanced; up to $5,000 only with Military certification.
notes.explanation: Noncash contributions of $500 or less are reported on Schedule A.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: Noncash contributions of $500 or less are reported on Schedule A and

notes.front: When is canceled nonbusiness credit card debt in scope?
notes.back: Only when the taxpayer was solvent before the cancellation (at Advanced).
notes.explanation: The insolvency exclusion is out of scope, even though the tax law allows it.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Nonbusiness credit card debt cancellation including interest in box 3 when taxpayer is solvent before the cancellation

notes.front: Which home-related cancellation of debt is in scope?
notes.back: Discharge of qualified principal residence indebtedness, at Advanced.
notes.explanation: It is the only exclusion from canceled debt income that is within the programmes' scope.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Temporary Provisions”, PDF p. 31
notes.evidence: Only cancellation of qualified principal residence indebtedness exclusion is within the scope of VITA/TCE.

notes.front: Besides credit card and principal residence debt, which cancelled debt is in scope on Form 1099-C?
notes.back: Certain student loan debt discharged in 2021 to 2025.
notes.explanation: Any other cancellation of debt is out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Discharge of certain student loan debt in 2021 through 2025

notes.front: When is Form 982 out of scope even for principal residence debt?
notes.back: When the taxpayer filed bankruptcy or was insolvent just before the cancellation, or the home was used for business or rental.
notes.explanation: Form 982 is in scope with Advanced certification only for qualified principal residence indebtedness.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: Principal residence used in business or as rental property • Taxpayer filed bankruptcy or was insolvent immediately before the debt was canceled

notes.front: Who can prepare a return with income from renting out a house or room?
notes.back: A Military-certified volunteer, for an active duty taxpayer only; a home rented for under 15 days is not a rental activity.
notes.explanation: Rental income and expenses for non-military taxpayers are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Home rental (including Part I, lines 5-19) if military certified and income taxpayer is active duty military

notes.front: A taxpayer rented out their home for fewer than 15 days. What level does the return need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: Renting a personal residence for under 15 days is not treated as a rental activity.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (A/M) Rental income (Advanced when the dwelling is a personal residence and rented for fewer than 15 days)

notes.front: Which Schedule K-1 items are in scope, and at what level?
notes.back: Interest, dividends, capital gains and losses, and royalties with no expenses, at Advanced.
notes.explanation: Other income, deductions and credits on a K-1 are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: Taxable and tax-exempt interest income ◦ Dividend and Qualified dividends income ◦ Net short- and long-term capital gains and losses

notes.front: Which residential energy credit is in scope, and at what level?
notes.back: The energy efficient home improvement credit, Form 5695 Part II only, at Advanced.
notes.explanation: The clean energy credit in Part I is out of scope.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (A) Energy efficient home improvement credit (Form 5695, Part II

notes.front: Which certification do the Schedule 1-A deductions for tips, overtime and car loan interest need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The enhanced deduction for seniors on the same schedule is the Basic exception.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 Scope of Service, Schedule 1-A”, PDF p. 6
notes.evidence: S 1-A 13 Yes No tax on tips Advanced certification

notes.front: What are the main limits on the car loan interest deduction?
notes.back: Up to $10,000 per return, for a new passenger vehicle bought after 2024 and assembled in the United States.
notes.explanation: Used car purchases do not qualify, and the vehicle identification number must be on the return.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page EXT-9, 2025 Tax Law Changes”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: A deduction is allowed for up to $10,000 of interest on a qualified passenger vehicle loan used to purchase a passenger vehicle after 12-31-2024 (does not apply to used car purchases).

notes.front: Which certification does an amended return (Form 1040-X) need?
notes.back: Advanced.
notes.explanation: The amended return must still be in scope in its own right.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: F 1040-X Yes Amended U.S. Individual Income Tax Return Advanced certification

notes.front: The original return was out of scope. Can volunteers amend it?
notes.back: Only if the amendment brings it into scope.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491 tells volunteers to confirm this first when asked to help with an amendment.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Amended and Prior Year Returns”, PDF p. 343
notes.evidence: first confirm the original return is within the scope of the VITA/TCE programs or that it will be in scope after the amendment.

notes.front: Form 8615 (kiddie tax) needs Advanced. For which income is it in scope?
notes.back: Native Americans' per capita payments and Alaska residents' permanent fund dividends.
notes.explanation: Other kiddie tax situations are outside the listed scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: Native Americans receiving per capita payments • Alaska residents receiving permanent fund dividends

notes.front: When is Form 8814, the parent's election to report a child's interest and dividends, in scope?
notes.back: Only for Alaska residents' permanent fund dividends, at Advanced.
notes.explanation: The chart lists that single case under Form 8814.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: F 8814 Yes Parent’s Election to Report Child’s Interest and Dividends Advanced certification In scope

notes.front: Above what taxable income is the qualified business income deduction out of scope?
notes.back: Over $197,300 ($394,600 if married filing jointly).
notes.explanation: Only the simplified Form 8995 is in scope; Form 8995-A is not.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: Taxable income over $197,300 ($394,600 if MFJ)

notes.front: Which qualified business income form is in scope?
notes.back: Form 8995 (simplified computation); Form 8995-A is not.
notes.explanation: Publicly traded partnership income is also out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 23
notes.evidence: F 8995-A No Qualified Business Income Deduction

notes.front: Is the alternative minimum tax (Schedule 2, line 2) in scope?
notes.back: No. A return is out of scope if AMT applies.
notes.explanation: Form 6251 is used only to carry private activity bond interest; the return is out if AMT is actually due.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: Out of scope if AMT applies

notes.front: Are household employment taxes (Schedule H) in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The scope chart marks both Schedule H and Schedule 2, line 9 as not in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: S2 9 No Household employment taxes

notes.front: Is the Additional Medicare Tax (Form 8959) in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Schedule 2, line 11 is marked not in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: S2 11 No Additional Medicare Tax

notes.front: Is the net investment income tax (Form 8960) in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Schedule 2, line 12 is marked not in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: S2 12 No Net investment income tax

notes.front: Is Form 4562, Depreciation and Amortization, in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Schedule C and rental returns that need Form 4562 are out of scope too.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 19
notes.evidence: F 4562 No Depreciation and Amortization (including information on listed property)

notes.front: Is Form 4684, Casualties and Thefts, in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Casualty and theft losses are also excluded from Schedule A.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 19
notes.evidence: F 4684 No Casualties and Thefts

notes.front: Is installment sales income (Form 6252) in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Installment sales are also listed as out of scope for Form 1099-S home sales.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: F 6252 No Installment Sales Income

notes.front: Is Form 709, the gift (and generation-skipping transfer) tax return, in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The scope chart marks Form 709 not in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: F 709 No United States Gift (and Generation-Skipping Transfer) Tax Return

notes.front: Are Form 8938 (specified foreign assets) and Form 3520 (foreign trusts and gifts) in scope?
notes.back: No, neither is.
notes.explanation: Schedule B is out of scope whenever either form is required.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 13
notes.evidence: Out of scope if FinCEN Form 114, F 3520 or F 8938 are required

notes.front: A rideshare driver has a Form 1099-K, $9,000 of expenses, the standard mileage rate and a net profit. What certification does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Schedule C and Form 1099-K self-employment income need Advanced. C is wrong because the business meets the Schedule C limits.
notes.explanation: Expenses under $50,000, the standard mileage rate and a profit keep the Schedule C in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: F 1099-K Yes Payment Card and Third Party Network Transactions Advanced certification In scope for:

notes.front: A cleaner's Schedule C shows $58,000 of business expenses and a profit. Can the site prepare it?
notes.back: C: no; expenses are not below $50,000.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Basic
B) Yes, at Advanced
C) No, it is out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because a Schedule C is in scope only with less than $50,000 in business expenses, whatever the certification.
notes.explanation: The expense limit is a scope limit, not a certification level.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: Volunteers can assist taxpayers who have returns that require Schedule C with certain limits: • Have less than $50,000 in business expenses

notes.front: A home baker buys ingredients to make and sell cakes and keeps stock between orders. She has no other issues. Is her Schedule C in scope?
notes.back: B: no; a business with inventory is out of scope.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Advanced
B) No, because of the inventory
C) Yes, if expenses are under $50,000
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong because having inventory at any time in the year takes the Schedule C out of scope, even when the other limits are met.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers with inventories are referred to a professional tax preparer.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Business”, PDF p. 106
notes.evidence: Inventory is the items the taxpayer buys or makes for resale to others. Taxpayers with inventories should be referred to a professional tax preparer.

notes.front: A taxpayer sold shares of stock she bought through a broker, and gives the basis. What does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced certification.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because selling shares needs Schedule D or Form 8949, which are Advanced. C is wrong because sales of stock are in scope.
notes.explanation: Stocks are one of the asset types in scope for Schedule D.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Interest and Dividends”, PDF p. 98
notes.evidence: A volunteer must have Advanced certification to prepare a return for taxpayers who sold mutual fund shares or other shares of stock.

notes.front: A taxpayer received a Form 1099-DA after selling bitcoin at a gain. What level can prepare the return?
notes.back: C: none; it is out of scope.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) It is out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because Form 1099-DA and digital asset transactions are out of scope at every level.
notes.explanation: Only a taxpayer who can answer No to the digital asset question stays in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: F 1099-DA No Digital Asset Proceeds From Broker Transactions

notes.front: A single taxpayer sold the home she lived in for ten years and never rented out, and received Form 1099-S. What does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced certification.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Form 1099-S needs Advanced. C is wrong because a personal residence sale is in scope.
notes.explanation: Rental use or a reduced exclusion would have put it out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 18
notes.evidence: F 1099-S Yes Proceeds from Real Estate Transactions Advanced certification In scope for: required • Personal residence

notes.front: A retiree's Form 1099-R leaves the taxable amount blank with box 2b checked; he made after-tax contributions. What does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced, which works out the taxable part with the Simplified Method.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Basic applies only when the taxable amount is shown. C is wrong because the Simplified Method calculation is in scope.
notes.explanation: The Simplified Method recovers his after-tax cost over the monthly payments.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 136
notes.evidence: In general, if the taxable amount is not indicated, volunteers with Advanced certification must calculate the taxable portion using the Simplified Method covered later in this lesson.

notes.front: A high earner covered by a workplace plan made a nondeductible traditional IRA contribution and needs Form 8606. Can the site prepare the return?
notes.back: C: no; nondeductible contributions and Form 8606 are out of scope.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Basic
B) Yes, at Advanced
C) No, it is out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because only deductible traditional IRA contributions are in scope, and Form 8606 is marked No.
notes.explanation: The IRA deduction line is in scope only for deductible contributions.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: F 8606 No Nondeductible IRAs

notes.front: A 40-year-old took an early IRA distribution and owes the 10% additional tax, with no exception claimed. What level does Form 5329 Part I need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B would apply only if an exception to the additional tax applied. C is wrong because Part I of Form 5329 is in scope.
notes.explanation: The level rises to Advanced only when an exception is claimed.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: S2 8 Yes Additional tax on IRAs, other qualified retirement plans, and other tax-favored Basic certification if accounts additional tax applies

notes.front: A family took HSA distributions during the year and bought Marketplace cover shown on Form 1095-A. What does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced certification.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Form 8889 and Form 1095-A both need Advanced. C is wrong because both are in scope within their limits.
notes.explanation: Two separate Advanced items appear on this one return.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: F 1095-A Yes Health Insurance Marketplace Statement Advanced certification required

notes.front: An itemiser gave $1,200 of used furniture to a charity. He is not in the military. Is the return in scope?
notes.back: C: no; noncash gifts over $500 are in scope only for Military certification.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Advanced
B) Yes, at Basic
C) No
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Advanced covers noncash gifts of $500 or less. B is wrong because Schedule A is never Basic.
notes.explanation: Up to $5,000 is in scope only with Military certification.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: Noncash charitable contributions up to $5,000 are in scope for Military certification only

notes.front: A taxpayer's credit card company cancelled $4,000 of debt. She was insolvent just before the cancellation and wants the insolvency exclusion. Is it in scope?
notes.back: C: no; credit card debt cancellation is in scope only if she was solvent before it.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Advanced
B) Yes, at Basic
C) No
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the insolvency exclusion is out of scope even at Advanced. B is wrong because Form 1099-C is never Basic.
notes.explanation: The tax law allows the exclusion, but volunteers may not prepare it.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Nonbusiness credit card debt cancellation including interest in box 3 when taxpayer is solvent before the cancellation

notes.front: A civilian rents a spare room to a lodger all year. An Advanced volunteer is on duty. Can the site prepare the return?
notes.back: B: no; rental income is in scope only with Military certification, for active duty taxpayers.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Advanced
B) No, it needs Military certification and an active duty taxpayer
C) Yes, if expenses are small
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Advanced covers only a personal residence rented for under 15 days. C is wrong because the amount does not change the rule.
notes.explanation: Rental income and expenses for non-military taxpayers are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Home rental (including Part I, lines 5-19) if military certified and income taxpayer is active duty military

notes.front: A homeowner installed new energy-efficient windows. What does the return need for the energy efficient home improvement credit?
notes.back: B: Advanced certification (Form 5695, Part II).
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because residential energy credits need Advanced. C is wrong because Part II of Form 5695 is in scope; only Part I is out.
notes.explanation: The clean energy credit in Part I would be out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: F 5695 Yes Residential Energy Credit Advanced certification Not in scope for: required • Clean Energy Credit (Part I)

notes.front: A waitress with tips on Form W-2 wants the no-tax-on-tips deduction on Schedule 1-A. What level does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because only the senior deduction on Schedule 1-A is Basic. C is wrong because the tips deduction is in scope.
notes.explanation: Her wages and tips alone would have been Basic; the deduction raises the level.

notes.front: A couple forgot a second Form W-2 on a Basic return that the site filed. Who can prepare their Form 1040-X?
notes.back: B: an Advanced-certified volunteer.
notes.choices:
A) Any Basic volunteer
B) An Advanced-certified volunteer
C) Nobody: amendments are out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Form 1040-X needs Advanced. C is wrong because amended returns are in scope when the return itself is.
notes.explanation: The original return was in scope, so the amendment can be done.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: F 1040-X Yes Amended U.S. Individual Income Tax Return Advanced certification

notes.front: A sole proprietor with an in-scope Schedule C has taxable income of $60,000 and qualifies for the qualified business income deduction. Is it in scope?
notes.back: A: yes, on Form 8995.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, on Form 8995
B) No, the deduction is always out of scope
C) Only on Form 8995-A
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because the 20% deduction for sole proprietors is in scope below the income limit. C is wrong because Form 8995-A is out of scope.
notes.explanation: Taxable income over $197,300 ($394,600 if filing jointly) would put it out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: The 20% deduction for sole proprietors and taxpayers with qualifying REIT dividends • Form 8995

notes.front: A retiree's large investment income makes her liable for the net investment income tax. Can the site prepare her return?
notes.back: C: no; the net investment income tax is out of scope.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Advanced
B) Yes, at Basic
C) No
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because Schedule 2, line 12 is marked not in scope at every level.
notes.explanation: The same is true of the alternative minimum tax, household employment taxes and the Additional Medicare Tax.

notes.evidence: S2 12 No Net investment income tax

notes.front: How does scope differ for deductible and nondeductible traditional IRA contributions?
notes.back: Deductible: in scope at Advanced. Nondeductible: out of scope, as is Form 8606.
notes.explanation: Roth IRA contributions, by contrast, are coded Basic on the intake sheet.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: S1 20 Yes IRA deduction Advanced certification In scope for: required • Deductible traditional IRA contributions Not in scope for: • Nondeductible traditional IRA contributions

notes.front: How does a home rented for fewer than 15 days differ in scope from a room rented all year?
notes.back: Under 15 days: Advanced, and not treated as a rental activity. All year: Military certification, active duty only.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C codes the item (A/M) for this reason.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (A/M) Rental income (Advanced when the dwelling is a personal residence and rented for fewer than 15 days)

notes.front: How does the scope of canceled credit card debt differ for a solvent and an insolvent taxpayer?
notes.back: Solvent before the cancellation: in scope at Advanced. Insolvent: out of scope.
notes.explanation: Insolvency is an exclusion the tax law allows, but it is outside the programmes' scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Nonbusiness credit card debt cancellation including interest in box 3 when taxpayer is solvent before the cancellation
